key_insight: A conservative Darcy–Brinkman–Stokes formulation (DBS2) naturally retains second-Brinkman effects through standard finite-volume central differencing, without separate discretisation.
engineering_relevance: DBS2 enables accurate flow and permeability prediction directly on voxelized rock images while preserving DBS1 computational efficiency.
method: Express the full DBS equation in conservative form.
Apply standard central differencing to retain second-Brinkman and porosity-gradient viscous terms.
Implement and validate DBS2 in GeoChemFoam, based on OpenFOAM.
evidence_signal: Across microchannel, 2D micromodel, and 3D Bentheimer sandstone benchmarks, DBS2 exactly reproduced the microchannel DNS velocity field and matched DNS permeability within 1.5–3.8% in the other cases; DBS1 overpredicted permeability by 14.1–37.9%.
watch_item: Validation covers three benchmarks at matched spatial resolution; accuracy on other rock geometries and coarser voxel grids remains to be established.
paper_title: A Conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes Formulation for Digital Rock Flow Simulation with Embedded Second-Brinkman Effects
